components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: How water moves between the oceans, the air and the land

components.text: The sun heats water in oceans, lakes and rivers. Some of the liquid turns into invisible water vapour and rises into the air. Plants add to this through transpiration, releasing vapour from their leaves.

components.title: Key idea
components.description: Evaporation is driven by solar energy. Warmer temperatures mean faster evaporation.

components.text: As water vapour rises, it meets cooler air and loses energy. It condenses into tiny liquid droplets around dust particles, and these droplets gather to form clouds.

components.title: Key idea
components.description: Condensation is the reverse of evaporation. Vapour cools and becomes liquid.

components.text: When cloud droplets grow heavy enough, they fall as rain, snow, sleet or hail. The water then runs off into rivers, soaks into the ground as groundwater, or returns to the oceans. From there the cycle starts again.

components.title: Remember
components.text: The water cycle has no start or end. The same water has been recycled for billions of years.

components.title: A Summer Day at a Mountain Lake
components.situation: On a hot July afternoon, a mountain lake loses water to the air. By evening, clouds build over the peaks and a thunderstorm drops rain on the slopes above the lake. Trace the path of one water molecule through the cycle.
components.model_answer: 1. Evaporation: the molecule absorbs solar energy at the lake surface and becomes vapour. 2. Condensation: it rises, cools at altitude and joins a cloud droplet. 3. Precipitation: the droplet grows and falls as rain on the slope. 4. Collection: runoff carries it down a stream and back into the lake.

questions.question: What primarily drives evaporation in the water cycle?
questions.explanation: Solar energy heats surface water and turns it into vapour.

questions.question: What happens during condensation?
options: Water vapour cools and turns into liquid droplets
questions.explanation: Cooling vapour loses energy and forms droplets, which gather into clouds.

questions.question: Which of these is a form of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Precipitation includes rain, snow, sleet and hail.
